hook.line: Vale says she'll talk about the menu, but not right now. Time to fix a day, a time and a place, the way people in Bogotá actually do it.
hook.es: ¿Nos vemos el viernes a las siete en el café?
hook.en: Shall we meet on Friday at seven at the café?

examples.es: ¿Nos vemos mañana a las diez en el parque?
examples.en: Shall we meet tomorrow at ten in the park?

examples.es: El viernes no puedo, ¿mejor el sábado?
examples.en: I can't on Friday, how about Saturday?

examples.es: Listo, el sábado a las ocho.
¿Nos vemos a la una en la plaza?
examples.en: Shall we meet at one in the square?

rule:
To suggest meeting, ask *¿Nos vemos…?* (literally 'do we see each other?') and add the pieces in this order: day, time, place.

Day: *el viernes* (this Friday). *Los viernes* would mean every Friday.
Time: *a las siete*, but *a la una*.
Place: *en el café*.

Can't make it? Say what doesn't work, then offer *mejor* plus another option: *El viernes no puedo, ¿mejor el sábado?*

To agree: *Listo* or *De acuerdo*.
smallPrint: In Spain people say *¿Quedamos?*; in Colombia *¿Nos vemos?* is the everyday way.

readAndPick.es: Listo, el sábado a las ocho.
options: The speaker says no to Saturday.
The speaker agrees to Saturday at eight.

readAndPick.es: A las siete no puedo, ¿mejor a las ocho?
options: The speaker suggests eight instead of seven.
The speaker suggests seven instead of eight.

readAndPick.es: ¿Nos vemos el domingo a las tres y media?
options: Shall we meet on Sunday at half past three?
Shall we meet on Sunday at three?
Shall we meet on Sundays at half past three?

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Shall we meet on Friday at seven at the café?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Nos vemos el viernes a las siete en el café?
yourTurn.why: Day, time, place: *el viernes*, *a las siete*, *en el café*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask: Shall we meet at one in the square?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Nos vemos a la una en la plaza?
yourTurn.why: One o'clock is singular: *a la una*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say you can't on Friday, and suggest Saturday.
yourTurn.answer: El viernes no puedo, ¿mejor el sábado?
accept: El viernes no puedo. ¿Mejor el sábado?
yourTurn.why: Say what doesn't work, then *mejor* plus the new day.

yourTurn.prompt: Agree with *Listo*: OK, Saturday at eight.
yourTurn.answer: Listo, el sábado a las ocho.
yourTurn.why: *Listo* is the everyday Colombian OK. The day keeps its *el*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask: Shall we meet tomorrow at ten in the park?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Nos vemos mañana a las diez en el parque?
yourTurn.why: *Mañana* takes no *el*, and the time still needs *a las*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say you can't at seven, and suggest eight.
yourTurn.answer: A las siete no puedo, ¿mejor a las ocho?
accept: A las siete no puedo. ¿Mejor a las ocho?
yourTurn.why: The same counter-offer works with times: *mejor a las ocho*.

yourTurn.prompt: Agree with *De acuerdo*: All right, see you there.
yourTurn.why: *Nos vemos* also closes the plan: see you there.

pitfalls.why: Days take *el*, not *en*: *el viernes* means 'on Friday'.
Clock times take *a*: *a las siete*, never *en*.
One is singular, so *a la una*.

personal: Arrange something real: suggest a day, a time and a place to meet a friend this week. *¿Nos vemos el… a las… en…?*
